I will keep my land in the usual `winter wheat + summer maize` rotation. In Quzhou County, this is the crop pattern I know best, it fits the local weather and water conditions, and it is the safest choice for me at my age because it is easier to manage with familiar machinery and ordinary field work. I will not spread myself into vegetables or other cash crops because they need more labor, closer management, and carry more market risk. I will use better seed, put most of my fertilizer into wheat and maize, irrigate when the crop stage matters most, and keep pesticide spraying limited to the times when disease, weeds, or insects are most likely. For wheat, I will focus on stable tillering, one good topdressing, and 2 to 3 irrigations. After wheat harvest, I will quickly sow summer maize, keep the stand even, feed it mainly with nitrogen, and protect it at the seedling and ear stages. My goal is steady yield and low risk, not chasing the highest possible output.
